sourceCopy.name: VO2 Max Calculator
sourceCopy.title: VO2 Max Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Estimate VO2 max with the Cooper run or Rockport walk test. Free browser calculator with clear method limits.
sourceCopy.intro: Estimate aerobic capacity from a 12-minute Cooper run or a one-mile Rockport walk. Select the method whose test you completed and enter its measurements.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How can I estimate VO2 max with a field test?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: The Cooper estimate uses distance covered in 12 minutes. The Rockport estimate uses a one-mile fast walk, age, weight, the equation’s male/female coefficient, walk time, and finishing heart rate. Each is a population-based prediction, not a lab measurement.
sourceCopy.privacyQuestion: Are my fitness test results uploaded?
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The estimate is calculated in this browser tab and is not uploaded or automatically saved.

fields.finishHeartRate: Heart rate immediately after the walk (bpm)
fields.protocolNote: Rockport protocol: walk one measured mile as quickly as you safely can; record the time and heart rate immediately at the finish. Do not run this test.
fields.accuracyNote: Field-test equations only estimate aerobic capacity. Results can differ from a supervised laboratory measurement and may not fit every person or population. No fitness category or diagnosis is assigned.
fields.safetyNote: The Cooper test is strenuous. Do not attempt a maximal effort if you are unwell, have symptoms, or have been advised to avoid vigorous exercise. Stop if you feel unwell; ask a qualified clinician about personal safety.
fields.privacyNote: Your entries stay in this browser tab. They are not uploaded or automatically saved.
fields.unitLabel: Milliliters of oxygen per kilogram per minute

messages.checkInputs: Check the test method and measurements.
messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is not available in this browser.

additionalFaqs.question: What does the Cooper test estimate use?
additionalFaqs.answer: It uses the distance covered during a 12-minute run. The estimate is a regression from a field test; it is not a direct oxygen-consumption measurement.

additionalFaqs.question: What measurements does the Rockport walk estimate need?
additionalFaqs.answer: The original equation uses a one-mile walk time, finishing heart rate, age, weight, and a binary sex coefficient. Its source study involved healthy adults ages 30–69; the result should not be treated as a universal prediction.

additionalFaqs.question: Is a VO2 max field-test estimate a medical result?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. It is an approximate fitness estimate and can differ from laboratory testing. It does not diagnose health or determine whether exercise is safe for you.
